title: Compiler admission keeps runtime and declared refusal codes unique
summary: Runtime refusal prefixes are reserved before admitting a thing’s automatic or explicit prefix. The existing refusal assembly rejects duplicate emitted codes, including a declared error colliding with the machine’s number 900. Invalid blueprints fail closed with an explicit-prefix recovery; nothing is silently renumbered.
proves: Actual Compiler.model rejects explicit AR, automatic article and archive prefixes, and the declared/machine AT-900 collision; it accepts article with explicit AT while retaining runtime AR-001. All compiler tests, compiler lint/typecheck and Nx sync check pass. No platform service is needed or started.

captions.01-fails-first: Four invalid code declarations unexpectedly compile before the fix; the valid custom prefix already passes.
captions.02-compiler-tests: Five admission regressions and all existing compiler tests, through the public compiler interface.
captions.03-static: Nx reset, sync, compiler lint/typecheck, sync check and whitespace validation.
